   CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS

  POLICY AND MANAGEMENT

  MEMORANDUM

TO:  October 7 Monument Ad Hoc Committee

FROM:  Nancy Hunt Coffey, City Manager
  Cynthia Owens, Municipal Affairs Program Manager

DATE:  August 12, 2024

SUBJECT:  Consideration of a Permanent Memorial for the Victims of October 7th
  Attack in Israel

ATTACHMENT:  1. Study Session Report - June 27, 2024

INTRODUCTION
On June 27, 2024, the City Council voted to establish an October 7 Monument Ad Hoc to
discuss and provide recommendations to the City Council on various means to memorialize the
victims of the October 7, 2023, Hamas attack on Israel. Ideas mentioned at this meeting
include:
  1) Potentially installing a temporary display/monument for October 7, 2024 while a more
  permanent monument proceeds through the process of being conceptualized;
  2) Determining a location for a permanent monument;
  3) Developing a process for creating a permanent memorial; and
  4) Honorary designation of a street and/or intersection;
  5) Establishing a process for collection of donations for the October 7 monument.

This item begins the initial process for the October 7 Monument Ad Hoc Committee (“Ad Hoc”)
to start exploring the areas mentioned above.

DISCUSSION
On June 27, 2024, the City Council discussed various ways the City could memorialize the
victims of the October 7, 2023, Hamas attach on Israel (Attachment 1). This report provides
many details for a temporary memorial, creating a permanent memorial, and providing an
honorary designation to a street for the events of October 7 which lead to the creation of this Ad
Hoc; therefore, the information will not be reiterated in this report.

Prior to discussion by the City Council, the Clerk advised there were over 3,100 emails received
on in support of the City creating a memorial in honor of those who lost their lives on October 7.
There was also extensive public comment made at the meeting in support of a memorial.

After comments and questions by the City Council, there seemed to be general support for:
  1) Temporarily reinstalling the flags in Beverly Gardens Park on October 7, 2024,
  displaying one national flag for each victim
  a. The question before the Ad Hoc would be to consider a time frame for the
  temporary installation such as 10 days or two weeks in October 2024. Once the
  time frame is agreed upon, staff would like to request a start date for the
  installation be recommended by the Ad Hoc.
  b. One Councilmember mentioned identifying a site for the permanent memorial
  prior to October 7. Then, on October 7 having a temporary memorial installed
   there which could be similar to the 9/11 memorial on the northwest corner of
  Rexford Drive and Burton Way. Prior the installation of the permanent memorial,
  there was a temporary display. No other Councilmember commented on this idea
  during the discussion. Staff is requesting the Ad Hoc consider this idea and make
  a final determination on whether or not this idea should be pursued in addition to
  the temporary flag display.
  2)  Creation and installation of a permanent memorial.
  a. The City Council appeared to have consensus for community participation in the
  design of the permanent memorial
  3)  Funding for the project should be through a community effort, similar to the 9/11
  memorial
  a. The Council seemed to indicate a 501 C (3) could be created and there appeared
  to be consensus on not listing the donors names on the memorial.
  4)  Allowing the Ad Hoc to explore safety and security concerns for the location of a
  permanent memorial. During the discussion of a location, some ideas mentioned at the
  June 27 meeting include:
  a. The area in front of the library on the northeast corner of Rexford Drive and
  Burton Way
  b. The public park on the southeast corner of Rexford Drive and Burton Way
  5)  Providing an honorary name to a street or intersection; however, no final determination
  was made by the City Council as to what street or intersection this could be

Additionally, at least two City Councilmembers felt there should be an educational component to
the October 7 Memorial; however, no other Councilmembers mentioned this so staff is seeking
direction from the Ad Hoc on including an educational component as part of the process for
creating a permanent memorial.

For refence of the Ad Hoc, memorial designs from the Oklahoma bombing, various 9/11
memorials, etc. are included as part of the Attachment 1 June 27, 2024 Study Session Report.

FISCAL IMPACT

Unknown. This is ultimately dependent on the direction received from the Ad Hoc and what the
City Council supports.

RECOMMENDATION:
Staff is requesting the Ad Hoc provide direction on any of the items mentioned in this report.

   STAFF REPORT

Meeting Date:  June 27, 2024
To:  Honorable Mayor and City Council
From:  Nancy Hunt-Coffey, City Manager

  Cynthia Owens, Municipal Affairs Program Manager

Subject:  Discussion on Memorializing the Victims of the October 7, 2023
  Hamas Attack on Israel

Attachment:  1. Memorial Examples

INTRODUCTION
This item provides the City Council an opportunity to discuss and provide direction on
means of memorializing the victims of the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack on Israel,
including reinstalling the flags in Beverly Gardens Park, a different short-term display or
memorial, the honorary designation of a street or intersection, and/or a permanent
memorial.

DISCUSSION
Background
On October 7, 2023, the Sabbath and a major Jewish holiday, Simchat Torah, Hamas
terrorists invaded as many as 22 locations in Israel. Hamas killed civilians and soldiers
while capturing at least 250 hostages. The attack also included firing thousands of
rockets as hundreds of Hamas fighters infiltrated the heavily fortified border in several
locations by air, land, and sea.

The Israeli cabinet unanimously approved the observance of a National Day of
Remembrance to commemorate the October 7 massacre and subsequent Gaza war, to
be held every year on the 24th of the Hebrew month of Tishrei. The annual memorial will
be marked by two state ceremonies honoring the memory of the servicemen and women
who fell in the ongoing war against Hamas and the civilians murdered during Hamas’s
brutal incursion. It will be held separately from Yom Hazikaron, Israel’s Memorial Day,
which is held on the 4th of Iyar.

After the events of October 7, the City Council took immediate action to recognize those
who were murdered and kidnapped. A shabbat table was placed at the front of City Hall
with a place set for each of the hostages who are unable to celebrate shabbat with their
family and friends. Flags were placed in Beverly Gardens Park to commemorate those
who lost their lives on October 7 — one flag representing the nationality of each
individual.
 Meeting Date: June 27, 2024

The City Council has additionally expressed a desire to commemorate October 7 for
2024 and in the future.

A number of ideas have been shared for ways to recognize what occurred. Some of
these ideas include:

  •  Reinstalling the flag display in Beverly Gardens Park. Feedback from the
  community was very positive regarding the flags, and some have indicated that
  they would like for them to be reinstalled. As discussed at earlier City Council
  meetings, the original goal was to get the flags installed quickly. As a result, the
  materials used were not intended for a lengthy installation. Should it be the
  desire of the City Council to reinstall the flags, staff recommends that the poles
  be replaced with a more durable material, such as PVC piping. Additionally,
  some of the flags have faded, so staff recommends that at least a few hundred of
  them be replaced.
  •  A short-term display or memorial. As October 7 is less than four months away,
  there has been an indication that a short term display could be installed which
  recognizes October 7. If this option is of interest to the City Council, staff
  requests additional direction on what a short-term display could entail.
  •  Provide an honorary designation to a City street or intersection which
  memorializes those who lost their lives in the October 7, 2023, attack or to
  rename an existing street. Additional details on this option can be found below.
  •  Creating a more permanent memorial to the victims of the attack. Some City
  Councilmembers have indicated a desire for such a memorial to be similar to the
  9-11 memorial located by the Fire Station at the northwest corner of Rexford and
  Burton Way. There have been suggestions for locating such a memorial near the
  City Hall campus. Should the City Council desire a permanent memorial, staff
  seeks Council direction on the design, scale, location, etc. Depending on these
  factors, it may not be possible to complete a permanent memorial by October 7,
  2024. Additionally, staff seeks feedback on whether the design of such a
  memorial should include a community outreach process and/or whether a
  fundraising campaign should be undertaken, similar to the 9-11 memorial.
  Additional conceptual information on more permanent memorials is included
  below.

Security - As a result of the shocking rise in Anti-Semitic acts across the globe and in the
United States, it is recommended that any memorial, temporary or permanent, be placed
in close proximity to the City Hall campus where sufficient BHPD and CCTV camera
coverage can act as a deterrent to any attempts at vandalism or defacement.

Street Naming – Honorary Designation or Renaming
The 2009 City Council Policy & Operations Manual addresses naming streets in the City.
Specifically, it states:
  • Street and sidewalk recognition – It is the City’s policy not to formally rename
  streets in recognition of an individual or business. On a case-by-case basis, the
  City Council may consider informal recognition of outstanding individuals and
  businesses with street and sidewalk plaques and signage.

Page 2 of 5
 Meeting Date: June 27, 2024

The City Council has previously recognized individuals for their contribution to the
community by approving the addition of names to streets or public alleys. Specific
examples include:

  1) June 2007 – The City Council designated the alley north of Wilshire Boulevard
  between Dayton Way and Rodeo Drive as Fred Hayman Place.

  2) February 2010 – In honor of Theodor Herzl, the City Council added the informal
  honorary designation of “Herzl Way” to the 300 block of North Clark Drive..

  3) October 2017 – The City Council designated the alley between the 400 block
  North Roxbury Drive and North Bedford Drive as Bram Goldsmith Way.

Staff seeks direction on whether an honorary street designation is the desire of the City
Council. If so, staff will return to a future meeting with suggestions on
streets/intersections where honorary street signs could be located. It should be noted
that the addition of an honorary street name designation does not change the official
street name; therefore, the process could be as simple as a resolution approved by the
City Council. However, if the City Council decide to rename a street, then this would be a
longer and more involved process. This includes a robust notification process including
but not limited to:
  • Notifying the impacted property owners of the potential street name change
  • Notifying impacted City resources such as Police, Fire, Community Development,
  and Public Works
  • Notifying impacted City billing departments
  • Notifying non-City entities such as Southern California Edison, Southern
  California Gas Company, and the United States Postal Service (USPS).
  • Conducting community outreach meetings
  • Presenting the proposal to one or more City Commissions for their consideration
  • Noticing and conducting public hearings
Page 3 of 5
 Meeting Date: June 27, 2024

The Beverly Hills Municipal Code (“BHMC”) does not specifically address renaming a
street, but it does address the naming of a street. Per BHMC 10-2-307 Street Names:

  Any street which is a prolongation or approximately a prolongation of an existing
  street shall be given the same name; otherwise no street shall be designated by
  the same name as that borne by any other street in the city, irrespective of the
  use of any suffix, such as "street", "avenue", "boulevard", "drive", "way", "place",
  "court", or other similar term. The planning official may recommend to the
  planning commission a change of the name of any street shown on a subdivision
  map or to designate a name when no name is shown. If the planning commission
  approves such recommendation or makes a different recommendation, any such
  recommendation shall be transmitted to the council for approval or disapproval.

Given the City Council Policy & Operations Manual as well as the City’s Municipal Code,
the City Council could consider:
  1) Providing an honorary designation to an existing street.
  2) Renaming an existing street

Memorial
As indicated above, some Councilmembers have expressed an interest in the creation of
a more permanent memorial to the victims of the October 7th attack. Various ideas for
what a memorial could look like are shown in Attachment 1 to this report. The memorials
in the Attachment are provided for context only and are not expressing a vision for what
the memorial may look like. Should the City Council wish to pursue a memorial, then the
City Council may wish to provide direction to staff on what the process for creating a
memorial should consist of and establish parameters for design and selection of an artist
to create a memorial, including the extent of a possible public engagement process for
the design, and direction on whether fundraising should occur to help pay for the cost of
the memorial, as was done with the 9-11 memorial.

As City Council considers the location of a possible memorial, it is helpful to consider
factors such as:
  • Public safety
  o Ability to close the street for annual memorial ceremony
  o Potential for demonstrations
  o Securing area to ensure memorial is not vandalized or defaced
  • Proximity to residents
  • Proximity to businesses

Staff also suggests the City Council consider a plaque, such as the one at Rexford mini
park, be installed at the memorial site to commemorate and explain the significance of
the memorial.

FISCAL IMPACT
The fiscal impact is unknown at this time as it would depend on the final direction of the
City Council.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends the City Council discuss the options provided above, as well as any
other ideas to memorialize the victims of the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack on Israel.
Page 4 of 5
 Meeting Date: June 27, 2024

After the discussion, staff is requesting the City Council provide direction on next steps
for the items mentioned in this report.

  Keith Sterling
  Deputy City Manager
  Approved By

Anthem Veterans Memorial
The Anthem Veterans Memorial is a monument located in Anthem, Arizona. On Veterans Day –

the precise alignment over the next 100 years to be between 11:10:58 and 11:11:22.

CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS
  455 North Rexford Drive
  Beverly Hills, CA 90210
  Video Teleconference
  Beverly Hills City Council Liaison / October 7 Monument Committee Meeting

  SPECIAL MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

  Monday, August 12, 2024
  11:00 AM

MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time:  August 12, 2024 / 11:00 AM
IN ATTENDANCE:  Mayor Lester Friedman, Vice Mayor Sharona Nazarian, City Manager
  Nancy Coffey, Municipal Affairs Program Manager Cynthia Owens, Fire
  Chief Gregory Barton, Police Chief Mark Stainbrook

  1) Public Comment:
  a. Leore Sassen via Zoom: He appreciates the efforts the City has undertaken to
  memorialize 10/7 and believes that it is beneficial for not only the city but also the
  United States as a whole.

  2) Consideration of a Permanent Memorial for the Victims of October 7th Attack in
  Israel:
  a. Presentation by Nancy Coffey:
  i. The City Council voted to establish the October 7 Monument Ad Hoc on
  June 27th, which was charged with exploring options for a permanent 10/7
  memorial.
  ii. The temporary flag memorial will be reinstalled from September 30th to
  October 14th in Beverly Gardens Park at Crescent and N Santa Monica
  Blvd.
  iii. The top expressed concern at the June 27th Council meeting was about the
  safety of the memorial and visitors.
  iv. The two proposed locations for the permanent memorial are at the
  Southeast corner of S. Santa Monica Blvd and Rexford in the mini-park, or
  at the Northeast corner of the same intersection in front of the library. The
  latter location was expressed as the preferred alternative by city staff.
  v. The Council also expressed their interest in a permanent honorary street
  name as well as an educational component to be a part of the memorial.
  vi. There is an art piece in front of the library that may need to be relocated
  depending on where the memorial is located.
  vii. The library location was preferred by staff for a multitude of reasons. Those
  being that the location does not back up into a residential neighborhood, it
  is close to the police station and fire station, it is adjacent to Civic Center
  Dr which can be easily renamed as part of a honorary street name, and
  that Civic Center can be easily closed should the City wish to hold an
  annual event at the site.
 Highlights for August 12, 2024
October 7 Monument Committee

  viii. There are several options for funding the monument such as community
  fundraising, creating a 501 (c) 3 specifically for the memorial, use the
  Community Charitable Foundation, or purely use City funds.\
  b. The 9/11 memorial was designed around a piece of steel from the Port Authority,
  and getting that steel was the aspect of the project that took the longest.
  c. The temporary 10/7 memorial will be discussed by the full council, not this
  committee.
  d. PD believes that either location would be fine in terms of the security of the area.
  e. Vice Mayor Nazarian expressed her interest in having some level of community
  involvement with the development of the memorial.
  f. City staff would like certain parameters to be put in place in terms of how the
  community is involved to prevent the memorial from being derailed by trying to
  accommodate too many varying opinions.
  g. An example of how the community could be involved in the process could be by
  selecting a set of commissioners that represent a broad range of opinions held by
  residents, while also holding several community meetings to get public feedback.
  h. The Vice Mayor would like to set the budget prior to sending out requests for artists.
  The city would then select three of those artists’ designs and have residents vote
  for which design they prefer.
  i. The 9/11 memorial cost around 375,000 to build.
  j. Both Liaisons favor the memorial to be in front of the library.
  k. The 9/11 memorial was designed from the ground up to be built around a piece of
  steel from the towers. This is in contrast to the 10/7 memorial, which has more
  flexible options.
  l. The Mayor believes that the City should replicate the funding model from the 9/11
  memorial for the 10/7 memorial.
  m. He is also in favor of an approach that has widespread community involvement.
  n. The Vice Mayor is open to having an artifact but would like that choice to be made
  early. She is opposed to having the artifact restrict the type of artists that can
  compete or needlessly bureaucratize the process. She also questions what types
  of artifacts can be used in a memorial display.
  o. The Mayor would like the idea of an artifact being a part of the memorial to be
  explored.
  p. The Vice Mayor is in favor of sending out an RFQ for the artist submissions.
  q. When the creation of a permanent 10/7 memorial was being discussed, there were
  over 3,500 emails sent in by members oof the public in support of the plan as well
  as the Council Chambers being packed with residents in support of a memorial,
  demonstrating how important this issue is for the community.
  r. The Liaisons are in favor of the RFQ budget ranging between $350,000 and
  $550,000.
  s. They are in favor of allowing the budget to potentially run higher than that.
  t. The City Manager believes that the RFQ application period should be between 4
  weeks to 2 months to allow time for it to reach artists who would then need to reach
  out about acquiring an artifact.

  3) Adjournment:
  Date / Time: August 12, 2024 / 12:11 PM
